- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/adr/*.md` are already clean as of #191 (the only remaining ADR hits are `0001:18` MD040, `0001:32` MD032, and `0002:28,113` MD034).

### 2. Commit-convention violations already on this branch

`CLAUDE.md` specifies gitmoji-prefixed Conventional Commits. Three commits don't comply, with real changelog consequences since `cliff.toml` sets `filter_commits = true`:

- `326673c meta(lint): ...` and `9039549 meta(config): ...` — `meta` matches no parser in `cliff.toml`'s `commit_parsers`, so both are dropped from the changelog entirely
- `f28e754 docs(adr): responses to PR feedback.` — no emoji, so it renders as `- Docs(adr): responses to PR feedback.`

Decide whether to rewrite the branch history before merge or accept the changelog gaps.

### 3. `LICENSE.md`'s new `# License` heading may break the license badge

`README.md:5` uses `img.shields.io/github/license/ebridges/wakil`, which relies on GitHub's `licensee`-based detection. Adding `# License` to `LICENSE.md:1` for MD041 may push the MIT text below `licensee`'s confidence threshold. Unverified — `licensee` wasn't run.

Either ignore `LICENSE.md` in the lint config (preferred) or use `# MIT License`, a title `licensee` recognizes and strips. Confirm the badge and the repo sidebar still read MIT after merge.

### 4. `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` entry ordering

Commit `326673c` relocated the 29.5-minute-enrich entry (2026-08-02) from the end of the file to ~line 39, bundled into a commit labelled "markdown lint fixes." The move is byte-identical and fixes no lint error, but the file's own header calls it an **append-only** log, and the result isn't date-ordered either: 08-05, 08-05, 08-02, 07-23, 07-18, 07-17, 07-09, 07-17, … with 07-28 entries near the bottom.

Either revert the move or do an explicit ordering pass in its own commit and document the intended order in the file's intro.

### 5. `## About` nests every entry beneath it

`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:9` and `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:9`. Every entry is an `###`, so adding `## About` makes the whole log a subsection of "About." No default markdownlint rule requires the heading. Either drop it or add a `## Entries` heading before the first entry.

### 6. `## Implementation` is "strongly preferred" but lives inside an HTML comment

`docs/adr/0000-template.md`. The copy instructions say to delete every HTML comment, so an author following them literally deletes the strongly-preferred section along with its guidance.

Suggested: promote `## Implementation` to a live heading with its guidance in a comment beneath it, and change the two genuinely-optional blocks (`Alternatives considered`, `Supersession relative to ADR NNNN`) to say "uncomment this section if it applies, otherwise delete it."

- `docs/adr/0000-template.md` cites pinpoint line numbers (0018 line 86, 0015 line 332, 0008 line 33, 0012 line 296). - `CLAUDE.md:33` — the `docs/adr/0000-template.md` bullet uses a hyphen where every sibling bullet in that block uses an em dash.
- `README.md` — "establishing how they're structured" wraps awkwardly and overstates the case; "new ADRs start from `docs/adr/0000-template.md`" reads better.



========== #190: enrich silently ignores explicit --context instructions to produce a required output page, and still reports success ==========
LABELS: bug
## What happened

A workspace has an established per-subject pattern: each source of a given kind produces three artifacts — a raw source note, an entity-page update, and a **separate typed page in a specific directory** (`<restricted-dir>/<subject-slug>-<kind>.md`, `type: assessment`). Eight prior sources of this kind all produced all three.

For the ninth, `enrich` was given unusually explicit instructions:

```
--context "... Follow the established pattern used for the other eight: raw
source under sources/, a <typed page> at <restricted-dir>/<subject>-<kind>.md
(type: assessment, ...), and a Timeline entry on <entity page>. See
<restricted-dir>/<other-subject>-<kind>.md for the exact shape."
```

Result:

```
Enriched source #N: 2 file(s) written, 7 candidate memories, 3 relationships.
  + <entity page>
  + <company page>
```

The third artifact was never proposed. No warning, no mention of the instruction, exit 0.

## Why this is worth fixing

The two pages it *did* write are good. The failure is invisible: `enrich` reports success, and the only way to notice the missing page is to know the pattern and check by hand. In a batch of sources that gap ships silently.

Note the contrast with the directory-validation path (#187), which *hard-fails* the whole run over a mechanically-correctable path error. Here a substantive, explicitly-requested output is dropped with no signal at all. The severity assignments are inverted.

## Possible angles

- If `--context` routing instructions are only advisory, say so in the docs — right now nothing suggests they can be silently dropped, and their presence in the prompt implies they're binding.
- Consider surfacing a summary of instructions the proposal did *not* act on, so the operator can see what was ignored.
- A stronger option: a way to *require* an output (e.g. `--require-page <path>` or `--require-type <type>`) that fails the run when unmet, for exactly this repeating-pattern case.
- Sibling-precedent awareness would help generally: eight existing files matching `<restricted-dir>/*-<kind>.md` is a strong structural signal that a ninth belongs there, independent of anything in `--context`.

## Workaround

Wrote the page by hand and committed it onto the ingest branch.


========== #189: No PDF ingest handler — ingest has transcript/text/article only, so PDFs need manual pdftotext and lose their real origin ==========
LABELS: enhancement
## Gap

`wakil ingest` offers `transcript`, `text`, and `article`. There is no handler for PDFs, which is a common capture format for papers, reports, and print/share exports of web articles.

## What the workaround costs

To ingest two PDFs I had to:

1. `pdftotext` each into a scratch file, and hand-clean extraction artifacts (ligature/small-caps splitting mangles running heads — an all-caps framework name came out as `S KILLW EAVER` throughout a 14-page paper, which would otherwise have been indexed and embedded in that broken form).
2. Hand-prepend a header block with title/author/date/URL, since none of that survives extraction.
3. `wakil ingest text <scratch-path>`.
4. Go back afterwards and hand-fix `origin:` in the committed clipping, because step 3 recorded the **scratch path** as the origin — a `/private/tmp/...` path that will not exist tomorrow.

Step 4 is the damaging one: without it the vault permanently records a dead temp path as the provenance of a source. It is easy to forget and there is no warning.

## Suggested behaviour

A `wakil ingest pdf <path>` that:

- extracts text with a layout-aware extractor and normalises the common artifacts (ligatures, hyphenated line breaks, split small-caps runs)
- pulls embedded PDF metadata (Title, Author, CreationDate) and any DOI/arXiv ID found in the text, using them to seed frontmatter and `origin:`
- falls back to the local file path for `origin:` only when nothing durable can be derived, and says so

## Smaller, independently useful fix

Even without a PDF handler: when `ingest text` is given a path under a temp directory (`/tmp`, `/private/tmp`, `$TMPDIR`), warn that `origin:` is being set to an ephemeral path and suggest passing an explicit origin. A `--origin <url>` flag on `ingest text` would let the caller set it correctly up front instead of patching the committed file afterwards.


========== #188: Entity-resolution 'update' targets a page that exists only on another unmerged ingest branch — silently skipped, so the second source about a topic can never enrich into it ==========
LABELS: bug
## What happened

Two sources about the same subject were ingested back to back. Each got its own ingest branch and draft PR, per design.

- Source #26 → branch A, PR A. Enrichment created `concepts/<the-page>.md` **on branch A**.
- Source #27 → branch B, PR B. Enrichment correctly resolved the same entity at 0.90 confidence, `central` relevance, action `update`, target `concepts/<the-page>.md`.

But enrich runs against the working tree, which is on `main`, where that page does not exist:

```
Entity resolution
┃ Entity          ┃ Type    ┃ Action ┃ Target                ┃ Conf ┃ Relevance ┃
│ <the entity>    │ concept │ update │ concepts/<the-page>.md│ 0.90 │ central   │

warning: <the entity>: entity resolution says update concepts/<the-page>.md,
but that file doesn't exist on disk — skipped
warning: Source 27 (...): enrichment produced no new page, stub, or update for
any entity — nothing will be written for this source.
Enriched source #27: 0 file(s) written, 15 candidate memories, 5 relationships.
No files were written; nothing to land.
```

Source #27 is now flagged enriched. Its 15 memories exist. But **no page content was written anywhere**, and the second source's genuinely unique material (in this case, author commentary that appears in the secondary source and not the primary) is not in any note.

## Why this is a real design gap, not just my usage

Branch-per-source is wakil's own model, and it is normal to ingest a cluster of related sources in one sitting before reviewing any PRs. In that situation every source after the first that resolves to a page created by an earlier unmerged source silently no-ops. The operator gets two warnings and an exit code of 0.

## Two separable problems

1. **Detection**: entity resolution matched against something (the index? the DB?) that knows about the page, while the writer checks only the working tree. Those two views should agree, or the mismatch should be surfaced as an error rather than a skip.
2. **Recovery**: there is no obvious way to say "apply this to the version on branch A" or "queue this update to reapply after PR A merges". `--force` does not help: nothing was written to update.

## Suggested handling

At minimum, exit non-zero with an actionable message naming the branch that holds the target file, so this doesn't pass as a successful enrichment. Better: detect that the target exists on an open ingest branch and offer to stack onto it, or record a pending update that re-runs after the merge.

## Workaround

None found that stays inside the tool. Landing the first PR before enriching the second source would work, but that inverts the intended review flow (PRs are meant to be reviewed by a human, later, in a batch), and requires knowing in advance which sources will collide.


========== #187: enrich proposes a type: source page under drafts/, which its own validator rejects — whole run hard-fails and writes nothing ==========
LABELS: bug
## What happened

`wakil enrich 27` ran to completion, produced 15 candidate memories and 5 relationships, then threw the entire result away because the page it had just written for itself violated its own routing rule:

```
Proposed note:
╭─ NEW drafts/techtalks-overview-how-to-build-ai-agents-that-can-handle-th.md ─╮
│ ---
│ title: "How to build AI agents that can handle thousands of tools (TechTalks…"
│ origin: article
│ url: https://bdtechtalks.com
│ ...
│ type: source
│ ---

Proposal failed validation — it cannot be applied:
  ✗ drafts/techtalks-overview-how-to-build-ai-agents-that-can-handle-th.md: type
    'source' pages belong under sources/, not drafts/
Nothing was written. Fix the gap (or re-run enrichment) and try again.
```

## The inconsistency

The proposal generator and the validator disagree about a rule the validator states flatly and mechanically: `type: source` → `sources/`. This is not a judgment call the model needs to get right — it is a pure function of the `type:` field.

Note that enrich **already auto-corrects the filename half** of the path when it disagrees with `slugify()`, emitting a `warning:` and proceeding. It should do the same for the directory half. A deterministic, single-valued correction is being treated as a fatal error instead.

## Expected

Either:

1. Auto-correct the directory from the schema's `directory:` for that `type` and emit a warning (symmetric with the existing slugify filename correction), **or**
2. Constrain generation so the directory is derived from `type` rather than chosen freely.

Failing the whole run and discarding the memories is the worst of the three options.

## Cost of the current behaviour

All model work for the run is wasted; the operator has to re-run enrichment (paying for it twice) and has no lever to fix "the gap" other than guessing at extra `--context` to steer the model away from `drafts/`.

## Workaround used

Re-ran with an explicit `--context` instructing it that `type: source` pages must live under `sources/`. The second run then proposed no page at all (for an unrelated reason — see the sibling issue about entity-resolution targets on other branches).


========== #186: enrich emits two near-duplicate pages for the same entity in a single run when slugify() renames one proposed path ==========
LABELS: bug
## What happened

A single `wakil enrich <id>` run on one source produced **two concept pages describing the same entity**, with byte-identical `name:` and `title:` frontmatter:

```
warning: Corrected the proposed note's filename from
concepts/compositional-skill-routing.md to
concepts/compositional-skill-routing-skillweaver.md to match slugify() (the same
convention new entity stub pages already use)
Enriched source #26: 2 file(s) written, 12 candidate memories, 5 relationships.
  + concepts/compositional-skill-routing-skillweaver.md
  + concepts/compositional-skill-routing-skillweaver-sad.md
```

Both files carried:

```yaml
type: concept
name: Compositional Skill Routing
title: "Compositional Skill Routing / SKILLWEAVER & SAD"
aliases: [<same four aliases>]
```

They were ~80% overlapping prose — same framework description, same statistics, same open threads, differently worded. Entity resolution had reported a single `create` action for one entity.

## Why it looks like a slugify interaction

The model appears to have proposed two paths for what it considered one entity (a general page and a technique-specific page). The slugify correction then rewrote one of them into a near-neighbour of the other. Whatever the origin, nothing downstream noticed that two proposed pages shared an identical `name:` + `type:` pair before writing both.

## Expected

Before writing, dedupe proposed pages by `(type, name)` — or at minimum by `(type, slugify(name))`. If two proposals collide, merge them or fail loudly. The slugify-correction step in particular should check whether its *corrected* path collides with another path in the same proposal set, since the correction is exactly what can create the collision.

## Impact

Silent duplicate entity pages in the vault, landed on a PR branch with a passing enrichment. Caught only by reading the diff. This is adjacent to but distinct from #170 (duplicates *across* `--force` retries) — this one happens within a single successful run.

## Repro sketch

Ingest a long technical document about one named framework that has a memorable sub-technique (framework X, technique Y), where the natural page title would be "X / Y". Enrich it.


========== #183: No way to delete/archive a source record via CLI or MCP ==========
LABELS: enhancement
## Problem

`wakil sources` (CLI) only exposes `list`, `show`, and `backfill-abstract` —
there's no `delete`/`archive`/`supersede` command. The MCP surface mirrors
this: `sources_list`/`sources_show` only, no mutation beyond
`ingest_apply`/`enrich_apply`.

Concrete case (kb-professional, 2026-08-05): two sources (Engineer B
#20, Engineer A #21/#22 — the latter itself a duplicate from #170) got
corrupted content committed against them during the concurrent-session
interference documented in #181/#182. The GitHub PRs were closable and the
git branches deletable, but the underlying `sources` rows have no supported
way to be marked dead/superseded — they just sit in `wakil sources list`
permanently, with `git_branch`/`git_pr_url` values pointing at branches/PRs
that no longer exist, and no way to distinguish "abandoned, redo happened
under a new source id" from "still needs attention."

## Fix direction

- `wakil sources archive <id> [--reason TEXT] [--superseded-by ID]` (or
  equivalent MCP tool) — soft-delete: keep the row for history but exclude
  it from default `list`/search-adjacent surfaces, and let `show` render an
  "archived, superseded by #N" banner.
- Worth considering whether `ingest_apply`/`enrich_apply` should offer an
  explicit "supersedes source #N" link when re-ingesting the same
  audio/meeting after a prior attempt is known-bad, so the relationship is
  queryable rather than just implied by matching filenames/dates.



========== #182: No isolation between concurrent wakil sessions sharing one working tree — commits/checkouts interleave and clobber uncommitted edits ==========
LABELS: bug
## Problem

Working on `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a` (kb-professional), I observed clear evidence that a second, independent process was operating against the exact same git working directory and `wakil` SQLite store at the same time as my own session:

1. **Duplicate ingest of the same source.** ~41 seconds after my own `wakil enrich 21 --force` finished, a second `wakil ingest transcript` commit (`7935c2a1`) appeared on a brand-new branch (`wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-with-engineer-a`, PR #26 in kb-professional), using the *same* scratchpad input file path I had used for my own ingest, and hitting the "-1" filename-collision suffix (#173) against the target path my own earlier ingest had already produced (`sources/transcripts/2026-08-04-transcript-note-engineer-a.md` → `...-1.md`). I never re-ran `wakil ingest transcript` myself. `gh pr list` confirms both PRs are real, both open, both about the same person (Engineer A), created 8 minutes apart.

2. **Uncommitted working-tree content changed under me repeatedly**, mid-task, on files I had just written and had *not yet committed* — e.g. `people/engineer-a.md` and `sources/transcripts/2026-08-04-acme-engineer-a.md` each came back with materially different content (different prose, different timestamps like "Duration: 00:29:21" vs my "00:33:48", different turn boundaries) than what I had just written, with no `git commit` of mine in between. `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` had to be used repeatedly to restore my own committed version before each subsequent commit.

3. **`git branch --show-current` changed without me running `git checkout`.** `git reflog` shows checkouts I did not issue (e.g. `moving from wakil/ingest/...-engineer-a to wakil/ingest/...-with-engineer-a`) interleaved with my own commands.

This points to two (or more) `wakil`-driven agent sessions sharing one on-disk working directory/clone with no isolation (no `git worktree`, no per-session lock), so each session's `git checkout`/`git commit`/file writes are directly visible to and can clobber the other's in-flight, uncommitted work. Anything one session commits and pushes is safe (git objects are immutable), but everything in between — working-tree edits, staged-but-uncommitted state, which branch is currently checked out — is a shared, unguarded resource.

## Fix direction

- If `wakil`'s design intends to support multiple concurrent sessions against one workspace root, each session should operate in its own `git worktree` (or an equivalent per-session clone/checkout) rather than sharing the single working directory that `wakil init` registers.
- Short of that, `wakil ingest`/`enrich` could at least take a lock (e.g. an advisory file lock under `.wakil/`) around the sequence of "checkout branch → write files → commit → return to prior branch," so two invocations can't interleave their checkouts/commits, and could detect "another wakil process appears to be active" and fail fast rather than silently interleaving.
- Worth an explicit note in workspace-level docs (and in any task/orchestration instructions that assume "one agent at a time, exclusive use of the working tree") that this is NOT currently guaranteed by wakil itself — today it's purely a scheduling/discipline convention the caller has to enforce out-of-band.

## Related

kb-professional PR #25 vs PR #26 (both "AI-mentoring 1:1 with Engineer A", same source content, 8 minutes apart) is the concrete duplicate this produced and needs manual reconciliation.



========== #181: enrich commits its changes onto main instead of the source branch, then leaves HEAD on an unrelated stale branch ==========
LABELS: bug
## Problem

Repro: on branch `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a` (created by a prior `wakil ingest transcript` run, source #21), ran:

```
wakil enrich 21 --force --yes
```

Output ended with:

```
Enriched source #21: 3 file(s) written, 6 candidate memories, 3 relationships.
  + people/engineer-a.md
  + companies/client-company.md
  + projects/client-company/ai-mentoring/client-company-ai-mentoring-program.md
Committed d437dba430 on wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a
PR: https://github.com/ebridges/kb-professional/pull/25
Returned to wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-with-engineer-g.
```

Two things are wrong here, both confirmed via `git log`/`git reflog`/`git branch --contains`:

1. **The commit `d437dba430` actually landed on `main`**, not on `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a` as the printed message claims. `git branch --contains d437dba430` returned only `main`. Local `main` ended up one commit ahead of `origin/main` (unpushed, luckily, so no bad merge occurred yet) — but this silently commits enrichment output directly onto the trunk, bypassing the PR/branch workflow entirely for anyone who doesn't independently check `git log main` afterward. Recovered by hand: `git cherry-pick d437dba430` onto the correct branch, then `git branch -f main origin/main` to reset the accidental commit off of main.

2. **The "Returned to ..." message checks out a completely unrelated branch** (`...-with-engineer-g`, a different person's in-progress ingest from earlier in the same session) instead of returning to `main` (like `wakil ingest transcript` does) or staying on the branch it just committed to. This leaves the working tree on a random stale branch with no relation to the just-run command, which is confusing and risks the next command in a script operating on the wrong branch.

## Fix direction

- `enrich` should commit onto the same branch the source's capture step created (or the branch that was checked out when `enrich` was invoked), never onto `main` regardless of what branch happens to be checked out when the internal git commit step runs.
- After committing, `enrich` should return to a predictable branch — ideally the branch it just committed on (matching capture step's docstring: "Lands on the same branch/PR the capture step started"), not whatever branch was left checked out by some unrelated prior command in the same shell session.
- Given #170/#168 already document workspace/branch-tracking issues in this area, this may share a root cause — flagging as its own issue since the repro and blast radius (silent commits onto `main`) are distinct and more severe.



========== #180: ingest's PR-landing step resolves the wrong existing branch/PR, causing cross-contamination between unrelated sources ==========
LABELS: bug
## Problem

When `wakil ingest transcript` (or the branch/PR-landing step it shares with
`wakil enrich`) checks whether a PR already exists for the branch it just
created/computed, it appears to resolve an **unrelated** existing branch
rather than doing an exact match against the branch name it just used for
this source. The failure surfaced as a `gh pr create failed: ... already
exists` error citing a branch name that belongs to a completely different,
unrelated source/person.

Downstream, a subsequent `wakil enrich <source_id>` call for the *correct*
source somehow ended up with the repo checked out on that *wrong* branch,
with a different (unrelated) source's uncommitted enrichment output sitting
in the working tree — i.e. this isn't just a cosmetic error message, the
git-branch resolution genuinely diverges from the source's own recorded
`git_branch` DB field at some point in the ingest→enrich flow.

## Observed evidence (2026-08-04, kb-professional vault)

1. `wakil ingest transcript <engineer-b-scratchpad-file>` correctly captured
   source id 20, committed to a correctly-named new branch
   (`wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-w-engineer-b`), but
   then failed at the PR-creation step:

   ```
   Landing failed: gh pr create failed: a pull request for branch
   "wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-with-engineer-g" into branch
   "main" already exists:
   https://github.com/ebridges/kb-professional/pull/23
   The written files are still on disk for manual review.
   ```

   Note: `...-with-engineer-b` and `...-with-engineer-g` are unrelated
   branches for unrelated sources/people — there is no reason the
   Engineer B ingest should ever look up or reference the Engineer G
   branch/PR.

2. `wakil sources show 20` correctly reported the source's own `Git branch`
   field as `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-w-engine…`
   (the correct branch) — so the DB row itself was not corrupted.

3. Immediately after, running `wakil enrich 20 --force` (which per
   `--help` "lands on the same branch/PR the capture step started") resulted
   in the actual git working tree being checked out on
   `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-with-engineer-g` (the
   *wrong*, unrelated branch), with uncommitted local modifications to
   `companies/the-client-company.md` and `people/engineer-g.md`, plus an
   untracked `sensitive/the-client-company/engineer-g-ai-mentoring-assessment.md`
   — content that clearly belongs to a completely different source's
   enrichment output, not source 20's.

   (Caveat: a second, genuinely concurrent Claude Code session was also
   active against this same working directory/repo during this window, so
   it's possible the two symptoms above have partially independent causes —
   but the branch-name string cited in the PR-creation error in step 1 is
   real evidence of a wakil-side resolution bug regardless, since that
   error occurred on the very first `ingest` invocation before any
   possibility of a second session's git operations being involved.)

## Fix direction

Whatever code path does the "does a PR already exist for this branch"
check before calling `gh pr create` should look up by **exact** branch
name (the one just written to the source's own `git_branch` DB column),
not by a fuzzy/prefix/title-similarity match that can collide with a
different branch whose auto-generated name happens to share a long common
prefix (`wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-w...` in this
case). Given the collision-prone naming scheme (dates + truncated titles),
an exact-match bug here is likely to keep recurring across this vault's
current heavy one-person-per-branch ingest workload.

---

## 1. Layout of `src/wakil/`

### `app/` — services (the business layer)

### `integrations/`

Constants: `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL = "claude-opus-4-8"` (line 20), `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 8192`. Note the repo-root `skills/mcp-coordinator/SKILL.md` is separate and served as an MCP resource.

### `schema/`
- `schema/loader.py` (293) — entity-schema catalog. Precedence constants `SOURCE_OVERRIDE`/`SOURCE_KB_LOCAL`/`SOURCE_USER`/`SOURCE_BUILTIN` (28–31), `DEFAULT_SCHEMA_DIR`, `FieldSpec`, `EntitySchema`, `resolve_schema_roots`, `load_entity_schemas` (cached), `resolve_entity_schema`, `resolve_page_shape_template`.
- `schema/validate.py` (134) — `validate_frontmatter`, `known_types`, `schema_for`, `SchemaError`.
- `schema/entities/*.yaml` — 14 built-in types: assessment, company, concept, idea, index, journal, meeting, meta, organization, person, project, reflection, source.
- `schema/templates/` — `compiled-truth-timeline.md`, `single-occurrence.md` page shapes.

### `storage/`
- `storage/schema.py` (209) — SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM. Models: `User`(22), `Workspace`(30), `Source`(43), `Note`(67), `Memory`(82), `Relationship`(115), `IngestRun`(142), `QueryRun`(159), `EnrichmentCheckpoint`(175), `GitChange`(198). `utcnow()` helper at line 14.
- `storage/database.py` (104) — per-workspace SQLite engine, `open_session`, `init_db` (runs Alembic on open), WAL/concurrency handling.
- `storage/fts.py` (120) — FTS5 external-content tables + triggers over notes/memories/sources.
- `storage/migrations/` — Alembic `env.py` + versions `0001_baseline` → `0007_enrichment_checkpoint` (entity columns, source git tracking, content_hash unique, memory stance, nullable relationship FKs, enrichment checkpoint).

### `knowledge/`
- `knowledge/markdown.py` (100) — markdown discovery + frontmatter/hash extraction.
- `knowledge/wikilinks.py` (44) — pure `[[wikilink]]` target parsing.

### `mcp/`
- `mcp/server.py` (176) — `FastMCP` server. `build_server` (163), `run_stdio` (175). Registers `_register_coordinator_resource` (36, serves `COORDINATOR_SKILL_PATH = <repo>/skills/mcp-coordinator/SKILL.md`), `_register_read_tools` (54: status/search/query/memory_list/memory_show/relationships/sources_list/sources_show/skills_list), `_register_git_tools` (119: git_summary/git_history), `_register_write_tools` (131: `ingest_prepare`/`ingest_apply`/`enrich_prepare`/`enrich_apply` — the prepare/apply pairs from ADR 0018).
- `mcp/tools.py` (537) — the actual tool implementations, incl. `_land` (300) and `_refresh_qmd` (332).
- `mcp/proposals.py` (59) — `ProposalCache`, the in-process bridge holding a proposal between prepare and apply.

### `config/` & `ui/`
- `config/settings.py` (139) — `WorkspaceConfig` (pydantic). Constants `WAKIL_DIR = ".wakil"`, `CONFIG_FILENAME`, `DATABASE_FILENAME`, `QMD_DIRNAME`, `SPECIAL_FILES = ("README.md","AGENTS.md","RESOLVER.md")`. **`generated_directory: str = Field(default="drafts")`** at line 62 — this is the drafts dir. Worktree-aware `state_root`/`is_linked_worktree`. `find_workspace_root`, `is_initialized`.
- `config/registry.py` (52) — `~/.config/wakil/workspaces.yaml` name→root registry (XDG-aware).
- `ui/console.py` (717) — all Rich rendering: `print_enrichment_proposal`, `print_capture_proposal`, `print_schema_validation`, `print_skill_lint`, diff previews, etc. Console constructed at import time (relevant to the conftest color hack).

---

## 2. Git operations

**Low level — `/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/src/wakil/integrations/git.py`:**
- `_run_git(root, *args)` (31) — best-effort, returns `None` on failure. **`timeout=15`** (hardcoded, line 37).
- `_run_git_checked(root, *args, timeout: int = 60)` (46) — raises `GitError`. **Default timeout 60s.**
- `changed_files` (62), `create_branch` (68), `create_branch_from` (72), `branch_exists` (88), `checkout` (92), `checkout_new_tracking` (96), `fetch_branch` (102), `worktree_anchors` (109), `resolve_default_branch` (127), `stage_and_commit` (140 — `add --` then `commit -m` then `rev-parse HEAD`), **`push_branch` (147) with `timeout=120`**, `file_history` (151), `wakil_branches` (158), `inspect_git` (163 → `GitInfo`).

**GitHub — `/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/src/wakil/integrations/github.py`:**
- `gh_available()` (17), `create_pull_request(root, title, body, draft=False)` (21) **`timeout=120`**, `comment_on_pull_request` (43) **`timeout=60`**, `mark_pull_request_ready` (60) **`timeout=60`**. Errors as `GhError`.

**Orchestration — `/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/src/wakil/app/git_service.py`:**
- `COMMIT_PREFIXES` (41), `PHASES = ("capture", "enrichment")` (42), `COMMIT_EMOJI` (44).
- `commit_message(kind, description)` (80) → `"{emoji} wakil {kind}: {description}"`.
- `ingest_branch_name(root, title)` (86) → `wakil/ingest/<UTC date>-<slugify(title, max_length=40)>`, with `-1`, `-2`… suffixes while `git.branch_exists`.
- `ensure_clean_for_branch` (97), `commit_change` (111 — used by `schema migrate --commit`).
- `prepare_landing` (132) → `LandingContext`; resumes `Source.git_branch` via `_resume_source_branch` (248) or `_create_fresh_branch` (270). `abandon_landing` (166). `land_ingestion` (175) — commit, `_remember_source_branch`, `_land_pr`, `_record_change`, `_return_to_branch`.
- `_land_pr` (316) — push + create-or-update PR; **draft when `phase == "capture"`, marked ready + commented on `phase == "enrichment"`**; returns `None` (non-fatal) if `gh` unavailable or no remote.
- `_phase_comment` (306), `_record_change` (370 → `GitChange` row + `IngestRun` fields).

CLI callers: `_land_written_files` in `cli/main.py:333`; MCP caller: `_land` in `mcp/tools.py:300`.

---

## 3. Dates and timestamps — **all UTC, no local time anywhere**

- `storage/schema.py:14` — `def utcnow(): return datetime.now(UTC)`; used as `default=`/`onupdate=` for every `created_at`/`updated_at`/`last_indexed_at`/`started_at` column.
- **Capture-time dates** (`app/ingest_service.py`):
  - `_generate_capture_metadata:339` — `today = datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat()` fed into the capture prompt.
  - `_build_raw_file:3244` — `created = datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat()`; frontmatter `created:` / `retrieved:` and the filename prefix `f"{proposal.meeting_date or created}-{slug}"`.
  - `_transcript_metadata:3280` receives that `created`.
  - `retrieved_at=utcnow()` at line 368 on the `Source` row; `completed_at=utcnow()` at 412 and 2717.
- **Meeting/title dates** — `infer_meeting_date(file, text)` at `ingest_service.py:3146`: filename first (`_ISO_DATE_RE`, `_COMPACT_DATE_RE`), then first 5 lines of the text. No timezone involved (string extraction).
- **Whisper recording date** — `_WHISPER_EPOCH = datetime(2001, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)` (3043) + `_whisper_recorded_at` (3046); Apple reference-date seconds → UTC ISO.
- **Enrichment `today`** used for timeline entries / stub frontmatter / revisions: lines 1410, 1560, 1865, 2331, 2828, 2906, 2961 — all `datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat()`.
- **Source captured date for timeline fallback** — `prepare_enrichment` (`ingest_service.py` ~958): `captured_at = source.retrieved_at or source.created_at`, `.date().isoformat()` → `proposal.source_captured_date` (issue #77).
- `git_service.py:87` — branch-name date, `datetime.now(UTC).date()`.
- `memory_service.py:121-132` — confidence fading; naive `created_at` is coerced with `.replace(tzinfo=UTC)`, age computed against `datetime.now(UTC)`.
- `search_service.py:88` — `_parse_dt` parses stored ISO strings (no tz assumption).

Since everything is UTC, a user in e.g. UTC-7 capturing after 17:00 local gets tomorrow's date in filename/frontmatter — worth noting for date-related issues.

---

## 4. Destination path computation, slugify, `-1` collisions

- **`slugify(value, max_length=60)`** — `app/ingest_service.py:3157`. Lowercase, `[^a-z0-9]+` → `-`, strip `-`, truncate to `max_length`, `rstrip("-")`, fallback `"untitled"`.
- **`_unused_path(root, directory, base)`** — `app/ingest_service.py:3401`. Tries `<base>.md`, then `<base>-1.md`, `<base>-2.md`, … while `(root / path).exists()`. This is the only `-N` collision mechanism for files.
- **`_LEADING_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-?\d{2}-?\d{2}-?")`** — line 3143. Applied in `prepare_capture` (`stem = _LEADING_DATE_RE.sub("", file.stem) or file.stem`) and deliberately *not* re-applied in `_build_raw_file` (comment cites issue #79 about double-stripping collapsing a date-only stem to `untitled`).
- **Raw capture path** — `_build_raw_file` (3235): `directory = Path(config.ingest_directory) / RAW_DIRS.get(source_type, "clippings")`; `RAW_DIRS` defined at line 95. Base = `f"{proposal.meeting_date or created}-{slugify(slug_source)}"` → `_unused_path(...)`. `slug_source` is deterministic (filename stem / article title), **never** the model-generated title — this preserves content-hash dedup idempotency (ADR 0010).
- **Proposed-note path** — `_sanitize_note` (3317): rejects absolute paths, non-`.md`, paths escaping the root, **and existing paths**; on any of those it falls back to `_unused_path(root, Path(config.generated_directory), slugify(proposal.title))` i.e. **`drafts/`**. Otherwise `_reslug_proposed_note` (3363) re-derives the filename from `slugify(H1)` (preserving a leading date prefix), rewrites wikilinks pointing at the old path, and appends a `proposal.warnings` entry.
- **Stub entity paths** — `_build_stub_entities` (1525) / `_build_stub_or_skip` (1494) route into `schema.directory` by construction.
- **Branch-name collisions** — separate `-N` loop in `git_service.ingest_branch_name` (86).
- Also relevant: `_entity_attachment_dir` (2045) and `_normalize_new_embed_paths` (2054) for `![[embed]]` rewriting; `_resolve_entity_slug` (2769); `_deslug` (1894).

---

## 5. Frontmatter / schema validation

- **`schema/validate.py:33 validate_frontmatter(entity_type, frontmatter, kb_root)`** — returns `list[SchemaError]`, empty = valid. Rules:
  - Unknown `entity_type` → hard error listing known types.
  - Declared `type:` must match the expected type.
  - **Category rules**: `category == "identity"` must use `name` not `title`; `category == "document"` must use `title` not `name`.
  - **Origin sub-schemas**: `effective_fields = schema.fields | schema.origins.get(frontmatter["origin"], {})`.
  - Required-field presence via `_present` (90) — `None` and whitespace-only strings count as absent; kind checks via `_check_kind` (97) for `string`/`date`/`enum`/`list`/`ref`; `_is_date` (125) enforces `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`.
- **`type: source`** — `src/wakil/schema/entities/source.yaml`: `directory: sources`, `category: document`, `page_shape: single-occurrence`; required `title` + `captured` (date) + `origin` enum `[transcript, article, twitter, export, manual]`; optional `url`, `tags`, `created`, `abstract`; per-origin blocks for `article` (author/published/description), `transcript` (recording_url/company ref/meeting_date), `twitter`, `export` (readwise_id/readwise_updated). **Note the mismatch worth flagging:** the schema requires `captured`, but `_build_raw_file` writes `retrieved` (non-transcript branch) and `created`/`meeting_date` (transcript branch, via `transcript_frontmatter_template`). Also `origin` in the schema is an enum of source kinds, while `_build_raw_file` writes `origin` = the file path and `origin_kind` = the type.
- **Proposal gate** — `app/ingest_service.py:2572 validate_proposal(proposal, kb_root)`, composed of:
  - `_validate_proposed_files` (2473) — duplicate paths, missing `type:` frontmatter, schema errors, and **directory routing**: a page must sit at `schema.directory` or a subdirectory of it (hard stop, not auto-corrected).
  - `_validate_entity_updates` (2519) — merged content must still parse and validate.
  - `_validate_unroutable_creates` (2544) — `action == "create"` with no schema, or a schema with no `directory` (e.g. `index`), is a hard stop / dropped upstream.
  - `_entity_type_of` (2468) helper.
- **Drafts rules** — only two code sites: `config/settings.py:62` (`generated_directory` default `"drafts"`) and `ingest_service.py:3355` (fallback routing on invalid path or collision). Fixture `tests/fixtures/kb/drafts/rough-idea.md` exercises it.
- **Migration side** — `app/schema_migrate_service.py`: `FIELD_RENAMES` (29), `_FRONTMATTER_RE` (37), `_QUOTED_TYPE_RE` (38), `plan_schema_migration` (76), `_plan_file` (108), `apply_migrations` (202).
- **Frontmatter template for capture** — `transcript_frontmatter_template(config)` (`ingest_service.py:3196`) derives the template from the resolved `source` schema (ADR 0011, no more `SCHEMA.md`), mapped through `_KNOWN_FIELD_VALUES` (3216).

---

## 6. Test layout

```
tests/
  conftest.py                 (50 lines — only 3 fixtures, all defined here)
  fixtures/kb/                a small fixture knowledge base copied per-test
    README.md, SCHEMA.md, RESOLVER-less
    concepts/{claims-routing,graph-memory}.md
    drafts/rough-idea.md
    meetings/2026/2026-07-01-planning.md
    people/jane-doe.md
    sources/transcripts/notitle.md
  unit/       27 test modules
  integration/ 11 test modules (all CLI-level, via Typer CliRunner)
  evals/      runner.py + test_skill_evals.py
```

**`tests/conftest.py` fixtures:**
- `isolated_workspace_registry` (autouse) — sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` to tmp, deletes `WAKIL_WORKSPACE` and `WAKIL_SKILL_PATH`.
- `_no_real_qmd` (autouse) — monkeypatches `wakil.integrations.qmd.shutil.which` to `None` so no real `qmd` subprocess ever runs; tests that want qmd re-patch it themselves (`_patch_qmd` in `tests/integration/test_qmd_cli.py`).
- `kb_path` — `shutil.copytree(FIXTURE_KB, tmp_path/"kb")`.
- Module-level env normalization before any wakil import: pops `FORCE_COLOR`, sets `NO_COLOR=1` and `COLUMNS=200` (Rich `Console` is built at import time in `ui/console.py`, and 80-col wrapping breaks substring assertions).

**Markers / config** (`pyproject.toml`):
- `testpaths = ["tests"]`
- `markers = ["eval: live-model skill evaluations (real API calls; excluded by default, run with -m eval)"]`

`_populate_proposal_from_models` runs two DAG nodes:
- **Node 1 — extraction**: `_run_extraction` (1169) using the per-kind skill (`transcript`/`text`/`article` SKILL.md) + `ExtractionOutput`. Produces title, summary, key_points, `CandidateMemory`s, `CandidateRelationship`s, and an optional `proposed_note` run through `_sanitize_note`.
- **Node 2 — entity resolution**: `_run_entity_resolution` (1210), always invoked. Inside it, `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2)` at line 1275 runs entity updates and stub synthesis concurrently (ADR 0020). Sub-steps: `_candidate_entity_notes` (1117), `_run_entity_updates` (2205) with `_split_candidates_by_content_length` (2303) and `_MAX_BISECTION_DEPTH = 3` truncation bisection (ADR 0015), `_apply_entity_revisions` (2326), `_revise_candidates` (2373), `_build_stub_entities` (1525), `_synthesize_stub_content` (1780), plus the suppression chain (`_suppress_stubs_matching_updates` 1610, `_suppress_dated_record_stubs_matching_updates` 1659, `_suppress_proposed_note_matching_updates` 1714, `_suppress_duplicate_of_proposed_note` 1460, `_is_source_self_mirror` 1426), `_reconcile_entity_links` (1902), `_merge_entity_note` (2125) / `_insert_timeline_entry` (2018) / `_dated_timeline_entry` (1986).

**Checkpointing** (ADR 0020, migration 0007): `_checkpoint_content_hash(content_hash, context_digest, client.model)` (663), `_load_checkpoint` (675), `_save_checkpoint` (690), `_clear_checkpoints` (731, called when `force=True`), payload (de)serialization at 746–828. Progress reporting via the `on_progress: Callable[[str], None]` kwarg threaded from the CLI.

Then `validate_proposal` gates, and `apply_enrichment` (2684) writes files (`_write_new_proposed_files` 2604), applies updates (`_apply_entity_updates` 2619), persists memories (`_persist_candidate_memories` 2644).

Budget constants at the top of `ingest_service.py`: `MAX_SOURCE_CHARS = 24_000` (88), `RELATED_NOTE_LIMIT = 5` (89), `GUIDE_MAX_CHARS = 4_000` (90); `_COMPILED_TRUTH_TARGET_CHARS = 1400` (2766, ADR 0017); `_LOW_RELEVANCE = {"minor", "peripheral"}` (2196).

# wakil — Architectural Map

Root: `/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil`. Python 3.12+, Typer CLI, entry point `wakil.cli.main:app`. ~12.4k lines under `src/wakil/`.

---

## 1. Layout of `src/wakil/`

### `cli/` — Typer surface
- **`/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/src/wakil/cli/main.py`** (1655 lines) — the entire CLI. Root `app = typer.Typer(...)` at line 48, plus 11 sub-apps declared at lines 53–73: `ingest_app`, `git_app`, `memory_app`, `schema_app`, `skills_app`, `qmd_app`, `qmd_collection_app`, `sources_app`, `entities_app`, `mcp_app`.

Top-level commands: `init` (146), `status` (185), `index` (191), `relationships` (198), `search` (269), `query` (292), `enrich` (591), `version` (1649).
Sub-commands: `ingest transcript|text|article` (679/700/721); `sources list|show|backfill-abstract` (742/768/786); `entities compile` (923); `memory list|show|promote|reject|archive` (1073–1151); `schema migrate|validate|list|which` (1160–1292); `git summary|history` (1309/1339); `skills list|which|describe|validate|lint` (1360–1482); `qmd collection add|list|remove` (1524–1562), `qmd sync|embed` (1578/1609); `mcp serve` (1633).

Key private CLI helpers: `_resolve_workspace` (104), `_land_written_files` (333), `_refresh_qmd_index` (376), `_resolve_context_or_exit` (400), `_prepare_enrichment_or_exit` (419), `_confirm_and_apply_enrichment` (452), `_run_ingest` (479), `_resolve_oversized_compiled_truth` (831), `_memory_session` (1041), `_transition` (1057). Shared option annotations `_CONTEXT` (570), `_CONTEXT_FILE` (580), `_YES` (669), `_LOCAL` (670).

### `app/` — services (the business layer)
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `app/ingest_service.py` (3424 lines) | The whole capture + enrich pipeline: prepare/apply capture, prepare/apply enrichment, entity resolution/stubs/merge, transcript parsing, slugify, path routing, proposal validation, entity compilation. |
| `app/git_service.py` (401) | Branch/commit/PR lifecycle around ingest ("landing"), plus `git_changes` bookkeeping. |
| `app/workspace_service.py` (318) | `wakil init`, note indexing, `status` inspection. |
| `app/query_service.py` (123) | Grounded QA over the KB; writes `QueryRun` rows. |
| `app/search_service.py` (102) | FTS/QMD-backed workspace search; `SearchHit`, `search_workspace`, memory-hit ranking. |
| `app/memory_service.py` (136) | Memory lifecycle: list/show/promote/reject/archive + confidence fading. |
| `app/graph_service.py` (235) | Relationship-table traversal (ADR 0006 phase 2) backing `wakil relationships`. |
| `app/context_references.py` (220) | Expands `@file:` / `@url:` refs inside `--context`/`--context-file`; token-budget trimming (`MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS`). |
| `app/qmd_service.py` (80) | Collection planning/creation and index refresh over the `qmd` integration. |
| `app/schema_validate_service.py` (75) | Walks markdown files, validates frontmatter → `FileValidation`. |
| `app/schema_migrate_service.py` (235) | `wakil schema migrate`: field renames, plan/apply migrations. |
| `app/data/common_words.zip` + `.SOURCE.md` | Stopword corpus data asset. |

### `integrations/`
- `integrations/git.py` (178) — raw `git` subprocess wrapper.
- `integrations/github.py` (74) — `gh` CLI wrapper.
- `integrations/qmd.py` (320) — `qmd` binary wrapper: `qmd_search`, `parse_qmd_results`, `detect_qmd`, `qmd_list/add/remove_collection`, `qmd_update`, `qmd_embed`; `SEARCH_MODES = ("search", "vsearch", "query")`.
- `integrations/web.py` (63) — article fetch + readability text extraction (`fetch_article`).

### `llm/`
- `llm/client.py` (178) — `ModelClient` Protocol, `AnthropicClient`, `OpenAICompatibleClient`, `resolve_client()`. Constants: `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL = "claude-opus-4-8"` (line 20), `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 8192`. Errors: `ModelError`, `ModelTruncatedError` (carries `partial`, drives truncation-based batching per ADR 0015).
- `llm/schemas.py` (285) — Pydantic contracts for all model output + `complete_with_contract()` (line 242), a validate-with-one-retry loop; `ModelContractError` (21).
- `llm/prompts.py` (396) — prompt builders (query grounding, capture metadata, etc.).
- `llm/skill_loader.py` (77) — `load_skill(name, kb_root)` (cached), `build_system_prompt(skill, output_model)` which concatenates `BASE_SYSTEM` + SKILL.md prose + `model_json_schema()`.

### `skills/`
- `skills/resolver.py` (276) — precedence resolution (ADR 0001, first-match-wins): `resolve_roots`, `resolve_skill`, `discover_skill_names`, `find_shadowed_roots`, `default_context`, `parse_skill_path` (`WAKIL_SKILL_PATH`), `validate_skill_name`.
- `skills/models.py` (93) — `SkillMetadata`, `ResolvedSkill`, `SkillRoot`, `ResolutionContext`.
- `skills/lint.py` (268) — content-quality lint beyond structural validation.
- `skills/evals.py` (89) — `eval.json` scenario schema, `load_eval_file`.
- `skills/errors.py` (29) — skill error types.
- **Built-in skill catalog** (data, not code): `src/wakil/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (+ optional `eval.json`) for `article`, `content-synthesis`, `entity-compile`, `entity-enrichment`, `entity-resolution`, `entity-resolve`, `ingest-source`, `kb-commit`, `knowledge-query`, `knowledge-research`, `note-conformance`, `note-revision`, `note-routing`, `skill-authoring`, `source-ingestion`, `text`, `transcript`. Note the repo-root `skills/mcp-coordinator/SKILL.md` is separate and served as an MCP resource.

### `schema/`
- `schema/loader.py` (293) — entity-schema catalog. Precedence constants `SOURCE_OVERRIDE`/`SOURCE_KB_LOCAL`/`SOURCE_USER`/`SOURCE_BUILTIN` (28–31), `DEFAULT_SCHEMA_DIR`, `FieldSpec`, `EntitySchema`, `resolve_schema_roots`, `load_entity_schemas` (cached), `resolve_entity_schema`, `resolve_page_shape_template`.
- `schema/validate.py` (134) — `validate_frontmatter`, `known_types`, `schema_for`, `SchemaError`.
- `schema/entities/*.yaml` — 14 built-in types: assessment, company, concept, idea, index, journal, meeting, meta, organization, person, project, reflection, source.
- `schema/templates/` — `compiled-truth-timeline.md`, `single-occurrence.md` page shapes.

### `storage/`
- `storage/schema.py` (209) — SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM. Models: `User`(22), `Workspace`(30), `Source`(43), `Note`(67), `Memory`(82), `Relationship`(115), `IngestRun`(142), `QueryRun`(159), `EnrichmentCheckpoint`(175), `GitChange`(198). `utcnow()` helper at line 14.
- `storage/database.py` (104) — per-workspace SQLite engine, `open_session`, `init_db` (runs Alembic on open), WAL/concurrency handling.
- `storage/fts.py` (120) — FTS5 external-content tables + triggers over notes/memories/sources.
- `storage/migrations/` — Alembic `env.py` + versions `0001_baseline` → `0007_enrichment_checkpoint` (entity columns, source git tracking, content_hash unique, memory stance, nullable relationship FKs, enrichment checkpoint).

### `knowledge/`
- `knowledge/markdown.py` (100) — markdown discovery + frontmatter/hash extraction.
- `knowledge/wikilinks.py` (44) — pure `[[wikilink]]` target parsing.

### `mcp/`
- `mcp/server.py` (176) — `FastMCP` server. `build_server` (163), `run_stdio` (175). Registers `_register_coordinator_resource` (36, serves `COORDINATOR_SKILL_PATH = <repo>/skills/mcp-coordinator/SKILL.md`), `_register_read_tools` (54: status/search/query/memory_list/memory_show/relationships/sources_list/sources_show/skills_list), `_register_git_tools` (119: git_summary/git_history), `_register_write_tools` (131: `ingest_prepare`/`ingest_apply`/`enrich_prepare`/`enrich_apply` — the prepare/apply pairs from ADR 0018).
- `mcp/tools.py` (537) — the actual tool implementations, incl. `_land` (300) and `_refresh_qmd` (332).
- `mcp/proposals.py` (59) — `ProposalCache`, the in-process bridge holding a proposal between prepare and apply.

### `config/` & `ui/`
- `config/settings.py` (139) — `WorkspaceConfig` (pydantic). Constants `WAKIL_DIR = ".wakil"`, `CONFIG_FILENAME`, `DATABASE_FILENAME`, `QMD_DIRNAME`, `SPECIAL_FILES = ("README.md","AGENTS.md","RESOLVER.md")`. **`generated_directory: str = Field(default="drafts")`** at line 62 — this is the drafts dir. Worktree-aware `state_root`/`is_linked_worktree`. `find_workspace_root`, `is_initialized`.
- `config/registry.py` (52) — `~/.config/wakil/workspaces.yaml` name→root registry (XDG-aware).
- `ui/console.py` (717) — all Rich rendering: `print_enrichment_proposal`, `print_capture_proposal`, `print_schema_validation`, `print_skill_lint`, diff previews, etc. Console constructed at import time (relevant to the conftest color hack).

---

## 2. Git operations

**Low level — `/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/src/wakil/integrations/git.py`:**
- `_run_git(root, *args)` (31) — best-effort, returns `None` on failure. **`timeout=15`** (hardcoded, line 37).
- `_run_git_checked(root, *args, timeout: int = 60)` (46) — raises `GitError`. **Default timeout 60s.**
- `changed_files` (62), `create_branch` (68), `create_branch_from` (72), `branch_exists` (88), `checkout` (92), `checkout_new_tracking` (96), `fetch_branch` (102), `worktree_anchors` (109), `resolve_default_branch` (127), `stage_and_commit` (140 — `add --` then `commit -m` then `rev-parse HEAD`), **`push_branch` (147) with `timeout=120`**, `file_history` (151), `wakil_branches` (158), `inspect_git` (163 → `GitInfo`).

**GitHub — `/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/src/wakil/integrations/github.py`:**
- `gh_available()` (17), `create_pull_request(root, title, body, draft=False)` (21) **`timeout=120`**, `comment_on_pull_request` (43) **`timeout=60`**, `mark_pull_request_ready` (60) **`timeout=60`**. Errors as `GhError`.

**Orchestration — `/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/src/wakil/app/git_service.py`:**
- `COMMIT_PREFIXES` (41), `PHASES = ("capture", "enrichment")` (42), `COMMIT_EMOJI` (44).
- `commit_message(kind, description)` (80) → `"{emoji} wakil {kind}: {description}"`.
- `ingest_branch_name(root, title)` (86) → `wakil/ingest/<UTC date>-<slugify(title, max_length=40)>`, with `-1`, `-2`… suffixes while `git.branch_exists`.
- `ensure_clean_for_branch` (97), `commit_change` (111 — used by `schema migrate --commit`).
- `prepare_landing` (132) → `LandingContext`; resumes `Source.git_branch` via `_resume_source_branch` (248) or `_create_fresh_branch` (270). `abandon_landing` (166). `land_ingestion` (175) — commit, `_remember_source_branch`, `_land_pr`, `_record_change`, `_return_to_branch`.
- `_land_pr` (316) — push + create-or-update PR; **draft when `phase == "capture"`, marked ready + commented on `phase == "enrichment"`**; returns `None` (non-fatal) if `gh` unavailable or no remote.
- `_phase_comment` (306), `_record_change` (370 → `GitChange` row + `IngestRun` fields).

CLI callers: `_land_written_files` in `cli/main.py:333`; MCP caller: `_land` in `mcp/tools.py:300`.

---

## 3. Dates and timestamps — **all UTC, no local time anywhere**

- `storage/schema.py:14` — `def utcnow(): return datetime.now(UTC)`; used as `default=`/`onupdate=` for every `created_at`/`updated_at`/`last_indexed_at`/`started_at` column.
- **Capture-time dates** (`app/ingest_service.py`):
  - `_generate_capture_metadata:339` — `today = datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat()` fed into the capture prompt.
  - `_build_raw_file:3244` — `created = datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat()`; frontmatter `created:` / `retrieved:` and the filename prefix `f"{proposal.meeting_date or created}-{slug}"`.
  - `_transcript_metadata:3280` receives that `created`.
  - `retrieved_at=utcnow()` at line 368 on the `Source` row; `completed_at=utcnow()` at 412 and 2717.
- **Meeting/title dates** — `infer_meeting_date(file, text)` at `ingest_service.py:3146`: filename first (`_ISO_DATE_RE`, `_COMPACT_DATE_RE`), then first 5 lines of the text. No timezone involved (string extraction).
- **Whisper recording date** — `_WHISPER_EPOCH = datetime(2001, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)` (3043) + `_whisper_recorded_at` (3046); Apple reference-date seconds → UTC ISO.
- **Enrichment `today`** used for timeline entries / stub frontmatter / revisions: lines 1410, 1560, 1865, 2331, 2828, 2906, 2961 — all `datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat()`.
- **Source captured date for timeline fallback** — `prepare_enrichment` (`ingest_service.py` ~958): `captured_at = source.retrieved_at or source.created_at`, `.date().isoformat()` → `proposal.source_captured_date` (issue #77).
- `git_service.py:87` — branch-name date, `datetime.now(UTC).date()`.
- `memory_service.py:121-132` — confidence fading; naive `created_at` is coerced with `.replace(tzinfo=UTC)`, age computed against `datetime.now(UTC)`.
- `search_service.py:88` — `_parse_dt` parses stored ISO strings (no tz assumption).

Since everything is UTC, a user in e.g. UTC-7 capturing after 17:00 local gets tomorrow's date in filename/frontmatter — worth noting for date-related issues.

---

## 4. Destination path computation, slugify, `-1` collisions

- **`slugify(value, max_length=60)`** — `app/ingest_service.py:3157`. Lowercase, `[^a-z0-9]+` → `-`, strip `-`, truncate to `max_length`, `rstrip("-")`, fallback `"untitled"`.
- **`_unused_path(root, directory, base)`** — `app/ingest_service.py:3401`. Tries `<base>.md`, then `<base>-1.md`, `<base>-2.md`, … while `(root / path).exists()`. This is the only `-N` collision mechanism for files.
- **`_LEADING_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-?\d{2}-?\d{2}-?")`** — line 3143. Applied in `prepare_capture` (`stem = _LEADING_DATE_RE.sub("", file.stem) or file.stem`) and deliberately *not* re-applied in `_build_raw_file` (comment cites issue #79 about double-stripping collapsing a date-only stem to `untitled`).
- **Raw capture path** — `_build_raw_file` (3235): `directory = Path(config.ingest_directory) / RAW_DIRS.get(source_type, "clippings")`; `RAW_DIRS` defined at line 95. Base = `f"{proposal.meeting_date or created}-{slugify(slug_source)}"` → `_unused_path(...)`. `slug_source` is deterministic (filename stem / article title), **never** the model-generated title — this preserves content-hash dedup idempotency (ADR 0010).
- **Proposed-note path** — `_sanitize_note` (3317): rejects absolute paths, non-`.md`, paths escaping the root, **and existing paths**; on any of those it falls back to `_unused_path(root, Path(config.generated_directory), slugify(proposal.title))` i.e. **`drafts/`**. Otherwise `_reslug_proposed_note` (3363) re-derives the filename from `slugify(H1)` (preserving a leading date prefix), rewrites wikilinks pointing at the old path, and appends a `proposal.warnings` entry.

61	========== #190: enrich silently ignores explicit --context instructions to produce a required output page, and still reports success ==========
62	LABELS: bug
63	## What happened
64	
65	A workspace has an established per-subject pattern: each source of a given kind produces three artifacts — a raw source note, an entity-page update, and a **separate typed page in a specific directory** (`<restricted-dir>/<subject-slug>-<kind>.md`, `type: assessment`). Eight prior sources of this kind all produced all three.
66	
67	For the ninth, `enrich` was given unusually explicit instructions:
68	
69	```
70	--context "... Follow the established pattern used for the other eight: raw
71	source under sources/, a <typed page> at <restricted-dir>/<subject>-<kind>.md
72	(type: assessment, ...), and a Timeline entry on <entity page>. See
73	<restricted-dir>/<other-subject>-<kind>.md for the exact shape."
74	```
75	
76	Result:
77	
78	```
79	Enriched source #N: 2 file(s) written, 7 candidate memories, 3 relationships.
80	  + <entity page>
81	  + <company page>
82	```
83	
84	The third artifact was never proposed. No warning, no mention of the instruction, exit 0.
85	
86	## Why this is worth fixing
87	
88	The two pages it *did* write are good. The failure is invisible: `enrich` reports success, and the only way to notice the missing page is to know the pattern and check by hand. In a batch of sources that gap ships silently.
89	
90	Note the contrast with the directory-validation path (#187), which *hard-fails* the whole run over a mechanically-correctable path error. Here a substantive, explicitly-requested output is dropped with no signal at all. The severity assignments are inverted.
91	
92	## Possible angles
93	
94	- If `--context` routing instructions are only advisory, say so in the docs — right now nothing suggests they can be silently dropped, and their presence in the prompt implies they're binding.
95	- Consider surfacing a summary of instructions the proposal did *not* act on, so the operator can see what was ignored.
96	- A stronger option: a way to *require* an output (e.g. `--require-page <path>` or `--require-type <type>`) that fails the run when unmet, for exactly this repeating-pattern case.
97	- Sibling-precedent awareness would help generally: eight existing files matching `<restricted-dir>/*-<kind>.md` is a strong structural signal that a ninth belongs there, independent of anything in `--context`.
98	
99	## Workaround
100	
101	Wrote the page by hand and committed it onto the ingest branch.

104	========== #189: No PDF ingest handler — ingest has transcript/text/article only, so PDFs need manual pdftotext and lose their real origin ==========
105	LABELS: enhancement
106	## Gap
107	
108	`wakil ingest` offers `transcript`, `text`, and `article`. There is no handler for PDFs, which is a common capture format for papers, reports, and print/share exports of web articles.
109	
110	## What the workaround costs
111	
112	To ingest two PDFs I had to:
113	
114	1. `pdftotext` each into a scratch file, and hand-clean extraction artifacts (ligature/small-caps splitting mangles running heads — an all-caps framework name came out as `S KILLW EAVER` throughout a 14-page paper, which would otherwise have been indexed and embedded in that broken form).
115	2. Hand-prepend a header block with title/author/date/URL, since none of that survives extraction.
116	3. `wakil ingest text <scratch-path>`.
117	4. Go back afterwards and hand-fix `origin:` in the committed clipping, because step 3 recorded the **scratch path** as the origin — a `/private/tmp/...` path that will not exist tomorrow.
118	
119	Step 4 is the damaging one: without it the vault permanently records a dead temp path as the provenance of a source. It is easy to forget and there is no warning.
120	
121	## Suggested behaviour
122	
123	A `wakil ingest pdf <path>` that:
124	
125	- extracts text with a layout-aware extractor and normalises the common artifacts (ligatures, hyphenated line breaks, split small-caps runs)
126	- pulls embedded PDF metadata (Title, Author, CreationDate) and any DOI/arXiv ID found in the text, using them to seed frontmatter and `origin:`
127	- falls back to the local file path for `origin:` only when nothing durable can be derived, and says so
128	
129	## Smaller, independently useful fix
130	
131	Even without a PDF handler: when `ingest text` is given a path under a temp directory (`/tmp`, `/private/tmp`, `$TMPDIR`), warn that `origin:` is being set to an ephemeral path and suggest passing an explicit origin. A `--origin <url>` flag on `ingest text` would let the caller set it correctly up front instead of patching the committed file afterwards.

134	========== #188: Entity-resolution 'update' targets a page that exists only on another unmerged ingest branch — silently skipped, so the second source about a topic can never enrich into it ==========
135	LABELS: bug
136	## What happened
137	
138	Two sources about the same subject were ingested back to back. Each got its own ingest branch and draft PR, per design.
139	
140	- Source #26 → branch A, PR A. Enrichment created `concepts/<the-page>.md` **on branch A**.
141	- Source #27 → branch B, PR B. Enrichment correctly resolved the same entity at 0.90 confidence, `central` relevance, action `update`, target `concepts/<the-page>.md`.
142	
143	But enrich runs against the working tree, which is on `main`, where that page does not exist:
144	
145	```
146	Entity resolution
147	┃ Entity          ┃ Type    ┃ Action ┃ Target                ┃ Conf ┃ Relevance ┃
148	│ <the entity>    │ concept │ update │ concepts/<the-page>.md│ 0.90 │ central   │
149	
150	warning: <the entity>: entity resolution says update concepts/<the-page>.md,
151	but that file doesn't exist on disk — skipped
152	warning: Source 27 (...): enrichment produced no new page, stub, or update for
153	any entity — nothing will be written for this source.
154	Enriched source #27: 0 file(s) written, 15 candidate memories, 5 relationships.
155	No files were written; nothing to land.
156	```
157	
158	Source #27 is now flagged enriched. Its 15 memories exist. But **no page content was written anywhere**, and the second source's genuinely unique material (in this case, author commentary that appears in the secondary source and not the primary) is not in any note.
159	
160	## Why this is a real design gap, not just my usage
161	
162	Branch-per-source is wakil's own model, and it is normal to ingest a cluster of related sources in one sitting before reviewing any PRs. In that situation every source after the first that resolves to a page created by an earlier unmerged source silently no-ops. The operator gets two warnings and an exit code of 0.
163	
164	## Two separable problems
165	
166	1. **Detection**: entity resolution matched against something (the index? the DB?) that knows about the page, while the writer checks only the working tree. Those two views should agree, or the mismatch should be surfaced as an error rather than a skip.

301	========== #182: No isolation between concurrent wakil sessions sharing one working tree — commits/checkouts interleave and clobber uncommitted edits ==========
302	LABELS: bug
303	## Problem
304	
305	Working on `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a` (kb-professional), I observed clear evidence that a second, independent process was operating against the exact same git working directory and `wakil` SQLite store at the same time as my own session:
306	
307	1. **Duplicate ingest of the same source.** ~41 seconds after my own `wakil enrich 21 --force` finished, a second `wakil ingest transcript` commit (`7935c2a1`) appeared on a brand-new branch (`wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-with-engineer-a`, PR #26 in kb-professional), using the *same* scratchpad input file path I had used for my own ingest, and hitting the "-1" filename-collision suffix (#173) against the target path my own earlier ingest had already produced (`sources/transcripts/2026-08-04-transcript-note-engineer-a.md` → `...-1.md`). I never re-ran `wakil ingest transcript` myself. `gh pr list` confirms both PRs are real, both open, both about the same person (Engineer A), created 8 minutes apart.
308	
309	2. **Uncommitted working-tree content changed under me repeatedly**, mid-task, on files I had just written and had *not yet committed* — e.g. `people/engineer-a.md` and `sources/transcripts/2026-08-04-acme-engineer-a.md` each came back with materially different content (different prose, different timestamps like "Duration: 00:29:21" vs my "00:33:48", different turn boundaries) than what I had just written, with no `git commit` of mine in between. `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` had to be used repeatedly to restore my own committed version before each subsequent commit.
310	
311	3. **`git branch --show-current` changed without me running `git checkout`.** `git reflog` shows checkouts I did not issue (e.g. `moving from wakil/ingest/...-engineer-a to wakil/ingest/...-with-engineer-a`) interleaved with my own commands.
312	
313	This points to two (or more) `wakil`-driven agent sessions sharing one on-disk working directory/clone with no isolation (no `git worktree`, no per-session lock), so each session's `git checkout`/`git commit`/file writes are directly visible to and can clobber the other's in-flight, uncommitted work. Anything one session commits and pushes is safe (git objects are immutable), but everything in between — working-tree edits, staged-but-uncommitted state, which branch is currently checked out — is a shared, unguarded resource.
314	
315	## Fix direction
316	
317	- If `wakil`'s design intends to support multiple concurrent sessions against one workspace root, each session should operate in its own `git worktree` (or an equivalent per-session clone/checkout) rather than sharing the single working directory that `wakil init` registers.
318	- Short of that, `wakil ingest`/`enrich` could at least take a lock (e.g. an advisory file lock under `.wakil/`) around the sequence of "checkout branch → write files → commit → return to prior branch," so two invocations can't interleave their checkouts/commits, and could detect "another wakil process appears to be active" and fail fast rather than silently interleaving.
319	- Worth an explicit note in workspace-level docs (and in any task/orchestration instructions that assume "one agent at a time, exclusive use of the working tree") that this is NOT currently guaranteed by wakil itself — today it's purely a scheduling/discipline convention the caller has to enforce out-of-band.

552	
553	`wakil enrich`'s auto-generated meeting-note summary for a source included:
554

563	### [26:28] John Doe

568	```

572	### 2. Enrichment defaults to "he/him" for a person entity when nothing in the source specifies gender
573	
574	Enriching a source for `[[people/joe-doe]]` produced Compiled Truth / Timeline prose using he/him pronouns throughout ("his tenure", "He gave concrete... examples", etc). Joe Doe is a woman (confirmed after the fact by the source's own author); nothing in the underlying transcript states a gender either way — the raw ASR transcript has no gendered self-reference, and the participant's existing person-page didn't have a `pronouns`/`gender` field for the model to check. 575	- if an entity already has a stated `pronouns:`/`gender:`-equivalent field, use it rather than defaulting;
